encounters.title: A Family at the Fence
encounters.flavor: An orchard fence bows under apples too small to pick. Behind it a family stands among stubborn rows of vegetables, hands still, watching you come up the track. The youngest has set a bowl of water outside the gate, and none of the grown-ups will say whether she meant it as a welcome.

choices.label: Bow and ask for shelter
choices.intent: Bow at the gate and wait to be invited before you ask for a roof.
choices.risk: If they read you wrong, the gate stays shut.

success.text: The eldest returns your bow and lifts the latch. You sleep beside their hearth, and at first light he tucks a cloth parcel of bread and windfall apples under your arm for the road.

failure.text: Their courtesy holds, but only just. The gate closes, and you spend the last of the daylight walking the long way around the orchard, footsore and chilled by the time you find a dry ditch to sleep in.

choices.label: Study the fence first
choices.intent: Read the posts and latch for signs of a hurried defense before trusting the welcome.
choices.risk: Lingering at a stranger's fence can look like a threat.

success.text: The broken latch has been wired shut from the inside by someone in a hurry. You mend it properly before you say a word. The father watches, nods once, and passes a few apples and a heel of cheese over the rails.

failure.text: Your long look reads as a threat. The mother pulls the children indoors and bars the shutters, and you spend a cold, aching night against the fence with the wind at your back.

encounters.title: The Orchard Debt
encounters.flavor: At the edge of the orchard, a farmer strains to heave a water barrel onto her cart. One wheel sits crooked in the dust, and a storm is building over the hills. She has food enough to trade but not the strength to move her harvest alone, and she says plainly that she will owe whoever helps.

choices.label: Help lift the barrel
choices.intent: Put your back under the barrel and heave it aboard before the storm breaks.
choices.risk: A slipping barrel can crack ribs.

success.text: With a grunt and a crack of timber, the wheel settles and the barrel rides level. She fills your hands with dried fruit and a sack of meal, and tells you she will not forget it.

failure.text: The barrel slips and slams into your ribs. The cart rolls free and the harvest is saved, but you leave the farm bruised, carrying the small bag of dried apples she insisted you take.

choices.label: Mend the axle first
choices.intent: Fix the crooked wheel properly so the lift does not wreck the cart.
choices.risk: If the repair fails, the storm arrives first.

success.text: You wedge the axle with a pin pulled from a fence post, and the wheel runs true. The farmer loads you with food and a dry cloth against the rain, and calls it the first payment on her debt.

failure.text: The pin snaps under the load. You catch the axle before the cart tips and the crop is saved, but the iron opens your palm, and you are still binding it when the first rain comes down.

encounters.title: The Scarecrow's Lantern
encounters.flavor: By the grain shed, a lantern swings from the arm of a scarecrow, though the air is dead still. A thin line of footprints runs behind the barn, and across that path someone has strung fishing line at shin height. Whoever lit the lantern wants you looking at it.

choices.label: Cut the hidden line
choices.intent: Find the snare line, cut it, and confront whoever is waiting behind the barn.
choices.risk: One wrong step and the trap springs on you.

success.text: The line parts cleanly under your knife. A thin figure bolts from behind the barn and over the fence, dropping a pouch of stolen rations in the dirt. No one comes to claim it, so it goes into your pack.

failure.text: Your foot finds a second line you never saw. A board snaps up out of the dirt and cracks across your shins, and while you stagger, the thief disappears into the dark.

choices.label: Circle around the grain shed
choices.intent: Skirt the snare and cut off the intruder at the back fence.
choices.risk: The ground behind the barn is soft and undercut.

success.text: You come around the shed exactly where the thief least expects you, and he drops a sack of food to run. In the chase, the old shortcut by the ditch caves in behind you, and the road ahead will have to bend another way.

failure.text: The thief doubles back through the brush. You crash after the sound until your lungs burn and your legs give out, and you lose both the trail and the last of the light.

encounters.title: The Last Seed
encounters.flavor: A gardener kneels over a single green shoot pushing through cracked soil. She holds a tin of seeds the way others hold a prayer book, and she says these are the last she has. The well beside her is nearly dry. She asks for nothing except that you not trample what little is still alive.

choices.label: Offer some of your water
choices.intent: Pour from your own flask so the shoot can survive the dry week.
choices.risk: Water spilled in this dust does not come back.

success.text: You pour slowly while she guides the stream to the root. When the soil is dark and wet, she climbs down into her cellar and returns with a jar of preserved fruit she will not let you refuse.

failure.text: Your hand shakes and most of the water runs off into the cracks. She thanks you anyway, and means it, but your flask is lighter and the shoot is barely wet.

choices.label: Build a windbreak for the sprout
choices.intent: Stack stones around the shoot so the hot wind cannot tear it out.
choices.risk: The wind may rise before the wall is finished.

success.text: Your little stone wall holds against the first gust. Digging for its footing, you strike a sealed jar of old provisions someone buried long ago, and the gardener insists it is yours by right of finding.

failure.text: The wind comes back before you finish and knocks the stones flat. You lunge to catch the seed tin before it rolls into the well and split your knuckles on the rim.

encounters.title: Rope at Dawn
encounters.flavor: At dawn a bucket hangs halfway down the stone well, turning slowly over water black with reflected sky. Its keeper kneels beside a fraying rope and will not let anyone pull alone. Behind you, a second traveler waits with an empty cup, too tired to argue.

choices.label: Take the strain on the rope
choices.intent: Hold the bucket's weight yourself while the keeper splices the worn rope.
choices.risk: If the rope parts, it will take skin with it.

success.text: You lean back and hold. The keeper splices the fray, the bucket rises full, and she fills your flask before sharing the morning's flatbread with you and the tired traveler.

failure.text: The rope runs through your grip and burns your palm raw. The water is saved and the keeper fills your flask, but the wound throbs under its bandage all morning.

choices.label: Show the keeper a safer knot
choices.intent: Retie the rigging so it holds without anyone straining on the line.
choices.risk: A bad knot could drop the bucket down the shaft.

success.text: The knot bites and holds under the full weight. Soon the line runs as smoothly as a hummed tune, and the keeper presses a twist of dried meat into your hand.

failure.text: The new line snags on the stone and frays through. You trade some of your own food to a passing carter for a replacement rope, so the keeper is not left with nothing.

encounters.title: A Cup Offered
encounters.flavor: A traveler offers you the first drink from a polished tin cup, holding it out in both hands as if it were a ceremony. The water smells faintly of something bitter. She keeps her eyes on your face instead of on the cup.

choices.label: Ask what is in the cup
choices.intent: Thank her, then ask plainly what she has added before you drink.
choices.risk: The question may sound like an accusation.

success.text: She laughs, a little embarrassed. The bitterness is willow bark for aching joints, she says, and she shows you how to steep it. The dose she wraps for you eases the ache in your shoulders by nightfall.

failure.text: To her, the question sounds like an accusation. She tips the cup out onto the sand, shoulders her pack, and walks to the far side of the well without another word.

choices.label: Accept the offered cup
choices.intent: Drink as you are asked, trusting her hospitality over your doubts.
choices.risk: If the bitterness is poison, it will be a long night.

success.text: The bitterness fades, and a slow calm spreads through your sore limbs. The traveler nods, satisfied, and fills the cup again; it is willow bark, she tells you, good for the road.

failure.text: The herbs hit hard on an empty stomach. You make it behind the well before you are sick, and spend the afternoon shaking in the shade while she apologizes from a careful distance.

encounters.title: Marks Below the Water
encounters.flavor: Just above the waterline, fresh scratches cut beneath older carved circles, and more show pale under the surface. A lone watcher swears none of them were there yesterday. The well stones tremble whenever a cart rolls past, but the marks seem to shift even when the road is empty.

choices.label: Measure the shifted stones
choices.intent: Check the well's stonework for danger before anyone else draws water.
choices.risk: Loose stones may give way under your weight.

success.text: One foundation block has slipped a hand's width toward the shaft, and the road beside it is hollow underneath. You help the watcher stake out a detour, and the way ahead now swings wide around the well.

failure.text: Your foot loosens a cracked step. Stones crash into the shaft, a falling chunk bruises your shin, and a cloud of grit leaves you blind and coughing at the rim.

choices.label: Lower a weighted line
choices.intent: Sound the well's depth from the rim instead of climbing into its unstable throat.
choices.risk: The stones below may cut the line.

success.text: The weight stops on a shelf where no shelf should be. Your hook comes up snagged on a small brass fitting and a bundle of oilcloth-wrapped hardtack someone hid down there, and you back away from the rim.

failure.text: The line saws through on sharp stone, and the pouch of dried beans you tied on as a weight goes with it. Leaning after it, you slip on the wet stones and end up soaked and shivering.

encounters.title: The Two Empty Buckets
encounters.flavor: Two empty buckets stand beside the well, each painted with a different household's mark. The owner of the second has not come for it in three days. Rather than let that family go dry, an exhausted courier has been hauling water to both homes, and her shoulders shake under the yoke.

choices.label: Carry the water for the courier
choices.intent: Take up both buckets so the absent neighbor's share arrives along with the courier's.
choices.risk: The path is steep, and water is heavy.

success.text: You make both deliveries before noon while the courier sleeps in the shade. Both doors open to take the water, and one household sends you off with a loaf and a wedge of hard cheese.

failure.text: You trip on loose stone and one bucket empties into the dirt. You top it up from your own water skin so the household is not shorted, and walk on with less than you came with.

choices.label: Follow the second bucket's mark
choices.intent: Trace where the absent household went instead of only carrying their water.
choices.risk: Night falls fast out here, and the marks are faint.

success.text: The household's mark appears again on fence posts, then on stones, leading toward the refuge road. On the last marker stone, someone has tied a small ribbon, knotted tight, as if meant to be found.

failure.text: After dusk the marks seem to lead in circles. You walk until your feet bleed in your boots, then limp back to the well with fewer answers than you set out with.

encounters.title: The Gate Still Open
encounters.flavor: The refuge gate stands open, though the hour is late. Beneath the adobe arch, a smiling sister holds up a lantern and offers you stew and a bed. From inside comes the steady clack of plates being stacked, but no children's voices, though this is a house built to take them in.

choices.label: Enter with formal thanks
choices.intent: Thank the sister properly and accept her stew, keeping both your manners and your guard.
choices.risk: Charity here may come with strings.

success.text: The stew is hot and thick, and its warmth goes into your hands and then deeper. A novice brings extra bread for your pack and, unasked, the names of the roads nearby.

failure.text: A bell sounds inside before you finish eating, and the sister hurries you back out through the gate. Only on the road do you notice that your pack is lighter than when you set it down.

choices.label: Watch the gate before entering
choices.intent: Study who comes and goes beneath the arch before you trust the welcome.
choices.risk: Watching too closely is its own kind of insult.

success.text: You wait in the shadow of the wall and read the dust. Small tracks pass in under the arch far more often than they come back out. You say nothing and fix the pattern in your memory.

failure.text: Your staring is noticed. The sister's smile thins, the gate swings shut, and you spend the night outside the wall on cold ground, waking stiff and aching.

encounters.title: The Locked Dormitory
encounters.flavor: A narrow corridor smells of soap and polished wood. Through the keyhole of a locked dormitory door you can see stripped beds and a small wooden toy lying beneath an empty coat hook. A nervous novice says the room is being cleaned and asks you to go back to the refectory.

choices.label: Question the novice gently
choices.intent: Speak quietly, away from the others, so the novice can talk without being overheard.
choices.risk: One wrong word and the novice will say nothing more.

success.text: The novice glances down the corridor, then whispers that the roster of children has gone missing. A scrap of paper with a room number is pressed into your hand, and the novice hurries off before you can ask more.

failure.text: Footsteps come down the corridor. The novice retreats behind a practiced smile, and a senior sister walks you outside, keeping the supper parcel you had left in the refectory.

choices.label: Examine the old lock
choices.intent: Look for proof in the lock and hinges without making an accusation yet.
choices.risk: If you are caught, the whole refuge turns against you.

success.text: Caught in the hinge is a frayed scrap of ribbon, like the ribbons tied to marker stones along the refuge road. You work it free and tuck it away before anyone comes.

failure.text: Your pick jams in the old lock. A caretaker rounds the corner before you can work it loose, and you abandon it, wrenching your shoulder on the window ledge as you climb out.

encounters.title: A Crust for the Road
encounters.flavor: By the kitchen door, a tired sister presses a small parcel of bread into your hand, crusts and heels wrapped in cloth for the road. She says it is only what was left from supper, then glances back at the convent windows. She may simply be kind, or she may be afraid of being seen.

choices.label: Accept the bread with a bow
choices.intent: Take the gift with quiet thanks and ask nothing that could get her in trouble.
choices.risk: Even a thank-you may be seen from those windows.

success.text: Your quiet thanks seem to settle her. She tucks a second loaf into the parcel and, beneath it, a folded note in small handwriting: the eastern road is safer than it looks.

failure.text: A voice calls her name from inside. She pulls back before you can finish thanking her, and all you are left holding is a single crust, still warm.

choices.label: Offer to help in the kitchen
choices.intent: Repay the bread with an evening's work instead of questions.
choices.risk: The longer you stay, the more eyes find you.

success.text: You scrub the last pans beside her in silence. As you dry your hands, she whispers about a dormitory door that stays locked day and night, and wraps an extra crust for your trouble.

failure.text: You linger too long under watchful eyes, and the senior sisters turn you out after dark. The night is cold and sleepless, and you start the morning drained.

encounters.title: The Silent Bell
encounters.flavor: A bell tower rises over a swept courtyard, its rope hanging dead still. A caretaker tells you not to touch it; the bell, he says, has not rung in years. Through the open stairwell you can see the bronze bell above, and a gap in the mechanism where some part should hang.

choices.label: Ask why the bell never rings
choices.intent: Ask the caretaker about the bell rather than climbing the tower uninvited.
choices.risk: Some silences here are kept on purpose.

success.text: The caretaker says more than he means to: the clapper was taken down on orders from above. Then the caretaker's mouth sets hard, and he will not say another word about it.

failure.text: He calls the question impertinent, walks you out of the gate, and points you down the wrong lane. By the time you realize it, you have walked miles on sore feet, and the road ahead runs somewhere new.

choices.label: Climb up and inspect the bell
choices.intent: Slip up the stairwell to see the bell's mechanism with your own eyes.
choices.risk: The stairs are old, and someone may see you climb.

success.text: The bronze bell hangs whole and sound, but its clapper has been unbolted and carried off. Someone silenced it on purpose. You fix the tower in your memory and slip back down unseen.

failure.text: A rotten stair gives way under you. You catch the rail and wrench your arm, your knee strikes stone, and by the time you limp down, watchers are gathering in the courtyard below.
